tool.name: krepp dist
tool.description: estimate distances of query sequences to reference genomes
tool.command:
mkdir -p index_dir && tar -xf '$index' -C index_dir &&
krepp dist -i index_dir -q '$query' -o '$output' --num-threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} #if $output_mode == 'no_multi': --no-multi #elif $output_mode == 'summarize': --summarize #end if #if $filter: --filter #end if #if str($dist_max): --dist-max $dist_max #end if

param.name: index
param.label: Krepp index
param.help: Index archive produced by krepp index

param.name: query
param.label: Query sequences
param.help: FASTA or FASTQ file containing query sequences

param.label: Statistical filtering
param.help: Retain only hits statistically indistinguishable from the closest hit

tool.help:
**What it does**
Estimates distances of query sequences (e.g., reads) to reference genomes using a pre-built krepp index. Distances are akin to the number of mismatches one would obtain by alignment.
**Output**
By default, a tab-separated file with columns:
- **SEQ_ID**: query sequence identifier - **REFERENCE_NAME**: reference genome identifier - **DIST**: estimated distance (mismatch rate)
With **Summarize** mode, outputs a weighted count table:
- **REFERENCE_NAME**: reference genome identifier - **WEIGHTED_COUNT**: shared read count - **SEQUENCE_ABUNDANCE**: normalized abundance
**Options**
- **Multiple hits**: Report all reference hits per read (default) or only the best. - **Filter**: Retain only hits statistically indistinguishable from the closest hit. - **Max distance**: Cap the maximum distance reported.
@ATTRIBUTION@
